messages:
maureen: Heads-up: canary rollout 2026-03-18-rc3 paused — dashboard shows ~28-35% p95 latency spike on long-seq workloads. Link: https://perf.redwood/d/rl/canary-rc3

dinesh: saw the alert, thanks. Which commit range are we bisecting?

maureen: Started an initial bisect across the last two merges; suspecting the recent runtime matrix change + allocator tweak. Bisect running now.

anya: quick profiling from the canary node: more GPU memcpy stalls and a lot fewer fused attention kernels. Flamegraph attached to the perf dashboard.

cheng: note we also bumped default max_batch_size to 128 in PR#5412 last week — could increase tail latency for short requests if batching heuristics misfire.

ben: also saw KV cache hit-rate drop in that canary region — TTL tweak in PR#5401 may be expiring prefixes earlier. Cache miss + larger batches = worse overall perf for long sequences.

perf-bot: nightly-perf-suite failed on branch main — regression detected: p95_latency_longseq +32% (threshold 5%). See /artifacts/176812/summary.json

infra-bot: rollback pipeline triggered by canary pause. Staging/Canary traffic currently pinned to previous variant.

dinesh: bisect result: culprit appears to be merge 176af2c (runtime: kernel selection matrix + allocator fallback ordering). Reproduces locally with the long-seq microbenchmark.

anya: confirmed locally: switching back to old kernel-selection table returns fused kernel counts and latency to baseline. The allocator fallback reordered some buffers which increased memcpy for KV cache refills.

maureen: ok please open an immediate revert and a hotfix branch. Also add a canary check that gates on both p95 latency and kv-hit-rate.

cheng: will draft PR to revert the matrix change. Meanwhile I can tune batching heuristic to prefer smaller batches when seq_len > 2048, should reduce stragglers.

ben: I'll instrument KV cache warmup in perf tests. Current perf-suite doesn't snapshot cache state so misses get averaged out. Proposing a new microbenchmark that pre-populates the cache and measures steady-state p95.

anya: adding to that — the perf CI is flaky because we use p99 for some ops. Switch suggested: use p95 for latency gating and a separate throughput delta check. Less noisy and more actionable.

maureen: agreed. Can we add a short config snippet for the perf test so it's reproducible?

anya: yes — sample config I pushed to my repo:```
name: longseq_kv_warmup
warmup: 500
seq_lengths: [4096, 2048]
batch_policy: prefer_small_for_long_seq
metrics: [p95_latency, throughput, kv_hit_rate]
thresholds: {p95_latency: 1.05, throughput: 0.97, kv_hit_rate: 0.02}
```

dinesh: workflow: merge revert > run targeted microbenchmark in CI > wait for clean canary > resume rollout. Also add a short bisect playbook for oncall so next time we don't spend hours.

infra-bot: revert PR 5429 created and pipeline started. Canary pinned until green.

perf-bot: queued nightly re-run of perf-suite with new microbenchmark. Will post results when done.

ben: I'll open a follow-up to snapshot KV state and add a synthetic warmup stage to the CI harness. That should reduce noisy regressions caused by cache cold-starts.

cheng: PR to tune batching heuristic drafted (WIP). I lowered default max_batch_size for sequences >2048 and added a small jitter for bin packing.

anya: also adding a quick kernel-selection unit test to ensure fused-kernel preference for attention shapes we care about. Small but should catch matrix regressions earlier.

maureen: perfect. After revert lands and CI confirms, we'll run a brief post-release retro to tighten perf tests and update the rollout checklist. Please add notes to the retro doc.

dinesh: root cause summary for the retro: kernel-selection matrix change + allocator fallback reorder -> fewer fused kernels + extra memcpy -> KV cache misses amplified by larger batch defaults -> p95 spike on long-seq. Fix path: revert matrix, tune batching, add KV warmup microbenchmark, switch gating to p95 + throughput, add unit tests.

maureen: thanks everyone — great triage. Tagging for follow-ups: @dinesh for revert, @anya for perf tests, @ben for kv warmup CI, @cheng for batching heuristic. We'll close the retro once fixes land. :thumbsup:
